title: Configure PingID Multi-Factor Authentication
description: Verify that PingID and corporate MFA sign-in are working before continuing with access requests and VPN-enabled onboarding steps.
helpText:
The MFA setup process is normally completed during laptop provisioning or through your onboarding contact. Verify all of the following before marking this step complete:

• PingID is configured.
• MFA sign-in works correctly.
• Corporate resources are accessible.

When verification is complete, click Mark Completed.

title: Request E5 license access
description: Open the access request portal so the engineer can request the E5 license upgrade required for GlobalProtect VPN access and engineering development work.
helpText:
1. Click Request Upgrade.

2. Select your GE HealthCare email account.

3. Choose:
   New GEHC PC or MAC

4. Enter:

Requesting Microsoft E5 license upgrade to enable GlobalProtect VPN access and support engineering development activities on my GE HealthCare workstation.

5. Submit the request.

6. Wait for approval before continuing with VPN-related onboarding steps.

title: Verify GlobalProtect VPN access
description: Confirm that GlobalProtect connects successfully and that an internal GE HealthCare resource is reachable before continuing with secured onboarding steps.
helpText:
1. Open GlobalProtect.

2. Sign in.

3. Verify successful VPN connection.

4. Open an internal GE HealthCare resource.

5. Click Mark Completed.

title: Open Prisma Browser guide
description: Open the Prisma Browser guide so the engineer can use Prisma as a temporary fallback while waiting for VPN or E5 access.
helpText: Use Prisma Browser only if VPN or E5 approval is still pending. It is a temporary fallback, not a replacement for working VPN access.

title: Request Box access
description: Open the access request portal so the engineer can request Box access for file sharing and onboarding/team documents.
helpText: Typical flow: start an access request, choose application access, search for Box, add the request, review it, and submit. Mark this step completed once access has been approved and verified.

title: Open GEHC Confluence
description: Open the main Confluence landing page to check whether documentation access is already available.
helpText: Run this step first to verify access. If Confluence opens correctly, continue with onboarding. If access is denied, use the Confluence account creation/reactivation step.

title: Request Confluence account creation / reactivation
description: Open the internal Confluence request page used when Confluence access is missing or the account needs reactivation.
helpText: Suggested flow: choose Account Creation / Reactivation, search for Confluence Global SaaS, complete the request, and submit it. No attachment is normally required unless your team says otherwise.

title: Open Pulse support portal
description: Open Pulse so the engineer can search support articles, find internal guidance, or raise support requests.
helpText: Use Pulse for support articles, ticket flows, internal KBs, software setup guidance, and troubleshooting information.

title: Install Google Chrome
description: Install Google Chrome if it is not already installed. Chrome is used for standard onboarding bookmarks and browser-based resources.
helpText: The script checks whether Chrome is already installed. If not, it installs Chrome silently in the background. After installation, run the bookmark step.

title: Add standard Chrome bookmarks
description: Add standard engineering onboarding bookmarks to Chrome using the resource list in Data/resources.json.
helpText: This step reads bookmark-enabled entries from Data/resources.json and adds them to Chrome. If Chrome has never been opened before, open Chrome once and close it, then run this step again.

title: Open Default Apps settings for browser selection
description: Open Windows Default Apps settings so the user can set Chrome as the default browser in a supported way.
helpText: Modern Windows protects default browser settings, so this step opens the supported Settings page instead of forcing registry changes. Set Chrome as default here if desired.

title: Install Git and Git Bash
description: Install Git for Windows, including Git command-line tools and Git Bash.
helpText: Git is required for source-control workflows such as cloning repositories, branching, committing, pulling, and pushing code. The script checks whether Git is already available and installs it if needed.

title: Install Visual Studio 2026
description: Install Visual Studio 2026 using the main team configuration file.
helpText: This step uses Configs\vs2026.vsconfig. It downloads the Visual Studio 2026 bootstrapper, installs Visual Studio silently, and applies the workloads, components, and extensions from the config file. Run the app as Administrator before starting this step.

title: Install Visual Studio 2022
description: Install Visual Studio 2022 using the separate VS2022 configuration file. Use this only if a project or workflow still requires Visual Studio 2022.
helpText: This step uses Configs\VS2022.vsconfig. Visual Studio 2022 is optional because installing both VS2022 and VS2026 can take significant disk space and time. Use it only if your project or team requires it.

title: Install .NET SDK 10
description: Install the .NET 10 SDK required for development and build workflows.
helpText: This step expects Configs\Installers\dotnet-sdk-10.0.301-win-x64.exe. The script checks whether a .NET 10 SDK is already installed and runs the installer silently if needed.

title: Install Windows SDK
description: Install the Windows SDK if the machine does not already have the required Windows development kit components.
helpText: This step expects Configs\Installers\winsdksetup.exe. Some desktop, WPF, native, or build workloads may require Windows SDK components.

title: Install Notepad++
description: Install Notepad++ as an optional lightweight editor for quick text, config, XML, JSON, and log file edits.
helpText: Notepad++ is optional. After installation, use the Default Apps settings step if you want to associate .txt or other file types with Notepad++.

title: Install Visual Studio Code
description: Install VS Code as an optional lightweight editor for quick repository browsing, scripting, and general development tasks.
helpText: VS Code is optional and useful for quick editing, scripting, Git review, and lightweight development outside the full Visual Studio IDE.

title: Install GitExtensions
description: Install GitExtensions as an optional graphical user interface for Git repositories.
helpText: GitExtensions is optional. It can help engineers who prefer a visual Git client instead of using Git only from the command line.

title: Install KDiff3
description: Install KDiff3 as an optional diff and merge tool for resolving file differences and merge conflicts.
helpText: KDiff3 is optional. It is useful for comparing files and resolving merge conflicts. If your team prefers Araxis instead, use the Araxis request step.

title: Open ReSharper download page
description: Open the ReSharper download page. Use this if the engineer needs ReSharper and the team has confirmed licensing or installation requirements.
helpText: This is currently a guided step rather than a fully automated install. Replace it later with a corporate-managed installer if your team provides one.

title: Open Araxis Merge request page
description: Open the corporate Araxis Merge page for users who prefer Araxis as their diff and merge tool.
helpText: Use this if the engineer needs Araxis Merge instead of KDiff3. This may involve a corporate software request or license approval.

title: Open Default Apps settings for text editor selection
description: Open Windows Default Apps settings so the user can choose Notepad++ or another editor for text files.
helpText: Use this after installing Notepad++ if you want to associate .txt, .log, .json, .xml, or similar file types with it.

title: Apply future registry configuration placeholder
description: Run a placeholder script reserved for future registry-based workstation configuration.
helpText: This is intentionally a placeholder. Later, replace the script with real approved registry configuration steps when your team finalizes them.

title: Apply reviewed GE_Kretz registry baseline
description: Imports reviewed HKCU and HKLM GE_Kretz registry settings after creating backups.
helpText: Use only after the registry files have been reviewed. HKCU settings apply to the current user. HKLM settings require Administrator rights. The script creates backups before importing.
